corrections.claimed_speedup: README chart '7-Zip Compression Performance': unprofiled 3,140 KB/s; MicroProfiler 840 KB/s; AQtime 135 KB/s; Visual Studio Instrumenting Profiler 116 KB/s. Results are Windows-era; Linux support (-finstrument-functions) came later.

tier_reason: In docs/index.html (the source of the github.io page) a first-party table gives the runtime cost per log as Palanteer 19.2 ns, NanoLog 10.7 ns and spdlog 1250 ns, and compilation speed as 2800, 265 and 470 logs/s, all on an AMD Ryzen 7 5700U. The spdlog and NanoLog harness is not published and flags are not stated, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Docs table (1M-iteration loop logging one parameter, queue write only, AMD Ryzen 7 5700U): runtime cost per log is Palanteer 19.2 ns, NanoLog 10.7 ns, spdlog 1250 ns (the author says spdlog's own figures could not be reproduced). That is about 65x faster than spdlog and 1.8x slower than NanoLog (derived from page data); the README rounds this to ~50x. Compilation: 2800 logs/s versus 470 (spdlog, about 6x) and 265 (NanoLog, about 10.6x). The self-test on a Core i7-7600U (gcc, Linux) reports 6.1 ns per event trace; the README says ~25 ns per event and up to ~5M events/s recording.
corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 5700U (logger comparison); Intel Core i7-7600U (self-test suite)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc on Debian 10 for the self-tests (-O2 noted for code size and compile speed); flags for the logger comparison are not stated
corrections.caveats: First-party comparison. Only Palanteer's test program is public; the spdlog and NanoLog harness is not. It measures only the enqueue into the internal queue (no formatting or output). The spdlog figure is far from spdlog's own published numbers, as the author notes. The baseline is a logger, so the record fits the profilers category only in part. The viewer and Python module are AGPL-3.0-or-later; the instrumentation libraries are MIT.

notes: The README's ~50x and 6x match the docs table, whose exact figures give ~65x. The github.io docs are blocked, so I read the same file from the repo's docs/ folder via raw.githubusercontent.com. Last commit 2025-05-12, so stale is correct.
